verses.1:1: And Solomon the son of David grew strong over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and exalted him on high.
verses.1:2: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and to the commanders of hundreds, and to the judges, and to all the rulers before Israel, the rulers of the fathers' houses.
verses.1:3: And Solomon and all the assembly went to the high place that was in Gibeon, where the tabernacle of testimony of God was, which Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the wilderness.
verses.1:4: But David had brought up the ark of God from the city of Kiriath-jearim, because he had prepared a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.1:5: And the bronze altar that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the Lord; and Solomon and the assembly sought it.
verses.1:6: And Solomon offered there upon the bronze altar before the Lord, which was in the tabernacle, and he offered upon it a thousand burnt offerings.
verses.1:7: In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."
verses.1:8: And Solomon said to God, "What great mercy You have shown to David my father, and You have made me king in his place.
verses.1:9: And now, O Lord God, let Your name be confirmed to David my father, for You have made me king over a numerous people, like the dust of the earth.
verses.1:10: Now give me wisdom and understanding, and I shall go out before this people and come in; for who shall judge this great people of Yours?"
verses.1:11: And God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for wealth of possessions, nor glory, nor the life of adversaries, and have not asked for many days, but have asked for wisdom and understanding for yourself, that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king,
verses.1:12: wisdom and understanding I give to you; and wealth and possessions and glory I will give to you, such that none like you has been among the kings before you, nor after you shall there be the like."
verses.1:13: And Solomon came from Maba that is in Gibeon, that is in Jerusalem, from before the tabernacle of testimony, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.1:14: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he left them in the cities of the chariots, and the people were with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:15: And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars in Judea like the sycamore trees that are in the lowland in abundance.
verses.1:16: And the bringing forth of the horsemen for Solomon was from Egypt, and the price of the king's merchants: they went and bought them.
verses.1:17: And they went up and brought out from Egypt one chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty; and thus they brought them by their hands for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
verses.1:18: And Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:1: And Solomon gathered seventy thousand men, and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain, and the overseers over them were three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:2: And Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in,
verses.2:3: so behold, I his son am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to sanctify it to Him, to burn incense before Him, and for the continual showbread, and to offer burnt offerings continually in the morning and in the evening, and on the Sabbaths and on the new moons and on the feasts of the Lord our God; this is forever upon Israel.
verses.2:4: And the house that I am building is great, for great is our God above all the gods.
verses.2:5: And who is able to build Him a house, since heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot bear His glory? And who am I, building Him a house, except only to burn incense before Him?
verses.2:6: And now send me a wise man who knows how to work in gold and in silver, in bronze and in iron, and in purple and in scarlet, and who understands how to engrave engravings with the wise men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, which David my father prepared.
verses.2:7: And send me cedar, juniper, and pine timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon; and behold, your servants with my servants
verses.2:8: shall go to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house that I am building is great and glorious.
verses.2:9: And behold, to the workmen who cut the timber I have given wheat for food as gifts to your servants, twenty thousand kors, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand measures of wine."
verses.2:10: And Hiram king of Tyre spoke in writing and sent to Solomon, "Because the Lord loved His people, He has made you king over them."
verses.2:11: And Hiram said, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to David a wise son, versed in understanding and knowledge, who shall build a house for the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:12: And now I have sent to you a wise man, one who knows understanding, Hiram my father;
verses.2:13: his mother is from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre; he knows how to work in gold and in silver, and in bronze and in iron, in stones and timber, and to weave in purple and in blue and in fine linen and in scarlet, and to engrave engravings, and to devise every design—whatever you may give to him—along with your wise men and the wise men of David my lord, your father.
verses.2:14: And now the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine, of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
verses.2:15: And we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring it on rafts to the sea of Joppa, and you shall bring it to Jerusalem."
verses.2:16: And Solomon gathered all the men who were sojourners in the land of Israel, after the numbering with which David his father had numbered them; and there were found one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:17: And he appointed from among them seventy thousand burden-bearers, and eighty thousand stonecutters, and three thousand six hundred over the people.
verses.3:1: And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Amoria, where the Lord had appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
verses.3:2: And the building began in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.3:3: And these things Solomon began to build for the house of God: the length in cubits, according to the former measurement, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
verses.3:4: And the vestibule in front of the house had its length across the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its height was one hundred and twenty cubits; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
verses.3:5: And the greater house he paneled with cedar wood, and overlaid it with pure gold, and carved upon it palm trees and chainwork.
verses.3:6: And he adorned the house with precious stones for glory, and with gold, the gold from Parvaim,
verses.3:7: and he overlaid the house, and the walls, and the gateways, and the ceilings, and the doors with gold; and he carved cherubim upon the walls.
verses.3:8: And he made the house of the Holy of Holies: its length across the front, a width of twenty cubits, and the length twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with pure gold for the cherubim, to the amount of six hundred talents.
verses.3:9: And the weight of the nails, the weight of a single one, was fifty shekels of gold; and he overlaid the upper chamber with gold.
verses.3:10: And in the house of the Holy of Holies he made two cherubim, a work of wood, and overlaid them with gold.
verses.3:11: And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in length: the one wing of five cubits touched the wall of the house, and the other wing of five cubits touched the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:13: And the wings of the cherubim were spread out twenty cubits; and they stood upon their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
verses.3:14: And he made the veil of blue and purple and scarlet and fine linen, and wove cherubim into it.
verses.3:15: And he made before the wall two pillars, thirty-five cubits in height, and their capitals were five cubits.
verses.3:16: And he made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them upon the capitals of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and placed them upon the chains.
verses.3:17: And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left; and he called the name of the one on the right Establishment, and the name of the one on the left Strength.
verses.4:1: And he made the altar of bronze, twenty cubits in length, and the width twenty cubits, ten cubits in height.
verses.4:2: And he made the molten sea, ten cubits in diameter, round all around, and five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
verses.4:3: And beneath it was a likeness of calves; all around they surround it, ten cubits encompass the laver all around; they cast the calves in two kinds in their casting,
verses.4:4: by which they made them twelve calves: three facing north, and three west, and three south, and three toward the east; and the sea was upon them above, and their hindquarters were inward.
verses.4:5: And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was like the brim of a cup, carved with buds of a lily, holding three thousand measures; and he finished it.
verses.4:6: And he made ten lavers, and placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them the works of the burnt offerings and to rinse in them; and the sea was for the priests to wash themselves in it.
verses.4:7: And he made the ten golden lampstands according to their ordinance, and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
verses.4:8: And he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left; and he made one hundred golden bowls.
verses.4:9: And he made the court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court, and their doorframes overlaid with bronze.
verses.4:10: And he placed the sea at the corner of the house on the right side, facing opposite toward the east.
verses.4:11: And Hiram made the fleshhooks, and the firepans, and the grate of the altar, and all its vessels. And Hiram finished doing all the work which he made for King Solomon in the house of God:
verses.4:12: two pillars, and upon them the bowls for the capital upon the tops of the two pillars, and two networks to cover the tops of the capitals which were upon the tops of the pillars,
verses.4:13: and four hundred golden bells for the two networks, and kinds of pomegranates on each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were above the pillars.
verses.4:14: And he made the ten stands, and he made the lavers upon the stands,
verses.4:15: and the one sea, and the twelve calves beneath it,
verses.4:16: and the footed pots, and the scoops, and the cauldrons, and the fleshhooks, and all their vessels, which Hiram made and brought up to King Solomon in the house of the Lord, of pure bronze.
verses.4:17: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the thickness of the ground, in the house of Succoth and Anamesirdathai.
verses.4:18: And Solomon made all these vessels in exceedingly great abundance, for the weight of the bronze did not fail.
verses.4:19: And Solomon made all the vessels of the house of the Lord, and the golden altar, and the tables, and upon them the loaves of showbread,
verses.4:20: and the lampstands and the lamps of light according to the ordinance, and before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold,
verses.4:21: and their tongs and their lamps, and the bowls, and the incense dishes, and the firepans, of pure gold,
verses.4:22: and the inner door of the house into the Holy of Holies, for the golden doors of the house of the temple. And all the work which Solomon made in the house of the Lord was finished.
verses.5:1: And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father, the silver and the gold and the vessels; he put them into the treasury of the Lord.
verses.5:2: Then Solomon assembled the elders and all the rulers of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, which is Zion.
verses.5:3: And all Israel assembled to the king at the feast, which is the seventh month.
verses.5:4: And all the elders of Israel came, and all the Levites took up the ark,
verses.5:5: and the tabernacle of the testimony, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle; and the priests and the Levites brought it up.
verses.5:6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, and those who feared and those of them who were gathered together before the ark, were sacrificing calves and sheep, which could not be numbered and could not be reckoned for multitude.
verses.5:7: And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.5:8: And the cherubim had their wings spread out over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered over the ark and over its poles from above.
verses.5:9: And the poles projected out, and the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary; they were not seen outside. And they were there until this day.
verses.5:10: There was nothing in the ark except two tablets which Moses placed at Horeb, the things which the Lord covenanted with the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.5:11: And it came to pass when the priests came out of the holy place—for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves; they were not arranged by division—
verses.5:12: and all the Levites who were singers, belonging to the sons of Asaph, to Heman, to Jeduthun, and to his sons and to his brethren, clothed in fine linen robes, with cymbals and with harps and with lyres, standing opposite the altar, and with them one hundred and twenty priests sounding with the trumpets,
verses.5:13: that there was one voice in sounding the trumpets and in singing and in proclaiming with one voice to give thanks and to praise the Lord; and they lifted up their voice with trumpets and with cymbals and with instruments of song, and they said, "Give thanks to the Lord, for it is good, for His mercy endures forever." And the house was filled with a cloud of the glory of the Lord,
verses.5:14: and the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the presence of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
verses.6:1: Then Solomon said, "The Lord said that He would dwell in thick darkness.
verses.6:2: And I have built a house for Your name, holy to You and prepared to dwell in forever."
verses.6:3: And the king turned his face and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood by.
verses.6:4: And he said, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to David my father, and with His hands has fulfilled it, saying,
verses.6:5: 'From the day that I brought My people up from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house that My name might be there, nor did I choose a man to be a leader over My people Israel;
verses.6:6: yet I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.6:7: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.6:8: And the Lord said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, it was well that it was in your heart;
verses.6:9: nevertheless you shall not build the house, for your son who shall come forth from your loins, he shall build the house for My name.'
verses.6:10: And the Lord has established this word which He spoke, and I have succeeded in the place of David my father and have sat upon the throne of Israel, as the Lord spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel,
verses.6:11: and I have placed there the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord which He made with Israel."
verses.6:12: Then he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands;
verses.6:13: for Solomon had made a bronze platform and set it in the midst of the court of the sanctuary, five cubits its length, five cubits its width, and three cubits its height; and he stood upon it, and fell upon his knees in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven,
verses.6:14: and said, "O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven and upon the earth, keeping the covenant and mercy for Your servants who walk before You with a whole heart.
verses.6:15: You have kept for Your servant David my father the things which You spoke to him; You spoke with Your mouth and have fulfilled them with Your hands, as it is this day.
verses.6:16: And now, O Lord God of Israel, keep for Your servant David what You spoke to him, saying, 'There shall not fail you a man before My presence sitting upon the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way to walk in My name, as you have walked before Me.'
verses.6:17: And now, O Lord God of Israel, let Your word be confirmed, I pray, which You spoke to Your servant David.
verses.6:18: For will God truly dwell with men upon the earth? If heaven and the heaven of heaven will not suffice for You, then what is this house which I have built?
verses.6:19: Yet look upon the prayer of Your servant and upon my supplication, O Lord God, to listen to the supplication and the prayer before You today,
verses.6:20: that Your eyes may be open upon this house day and night, toward this place of which You said that Your name would be invoked there, to hear the prayer which Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.6:21: And hear the supplication of Your servant and of the people of Israel, whatever they pray toward this place; and You, listen in the place of Your dwelling, from heaven, and hear and be merciful.
verses.6:22: If a man sins against his neighbor, and takes upon him an oath to make him swear, and he comes and swears before the altar in this house,
verses.6:23: then hear from heaven and act, and judge Your servants, repaying the lawless one and bringing his ways back upon his own head, and justifying the righteous, repaying him according to his righteousness.
verses.6:24: And if Your people Israel are defeated before the enemy if they sin against You, and they turn back and confess Your name, and pray and make supplication before You in this house,
verses.6:25: then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land which You gave to them and to their fathers.
verses.6:26: When the heaven is shut up and there is no rain because they sin against You, and they pray toward this place and praise Your name, and turn from their sins because You humble them,
verses.6:27: then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of Your servants and of Your people Israel, for You will show them the good way in which they shall walk; and send rain upon Your land which You have given to Your people for an inheritance.
verses.6:28: If famine comes upon the land, if pestilence comes upon the land, if there is blight and mildew, locust and caterpillar; if the enemy oppresses them before their cities, in every plague and every distress,
verses.6:29: then whatever prayer and whatever supplication is made by any man and by all Your people Israel, when a man knows his own affliction and his own sickness, and spreads out his hands toward this house,
verses.6:30: then hear from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, and heal, and render to each man according to his ways, as You know his heart—for You alone know the heart of the sons of men—
verses.6:31: that they may fear all Your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the land which You gave to our fathers.
verses.6:32: Moreover, concerning every foreigner who is not of the people of Israel, who comes from a far country for the sake of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your uplifted arm, when they come and pray toward this place,
verses.6:33: then hear from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls upon You, that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name, and fear You as does Your people Israel, and know that Your name is called upon this house which I have built.
verses.6:34: And if Your people go out to battle against their enemies by the way that You shall send them, and they pray to You toward this city which You have chosen and the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.6:35: then hear from heaven their supplication and their prayer, and maintain their just cause.
verses.6:36: When they sin against You—for there is no man who will not sin—and You strike them and deliver them before enemies, and their captors carry them away captive to a land of enemies, to a land far or near,
verses.6:37: and they turn their heart in their land to which they were carried away, and turn back and make supplication to You in their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted lawlessly,'
verses.6:38: and they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of those who took them captive, and pray toward their land which You gave to their fathers, and the city which You have chosen, and the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.6:39: then hear from heaven, from Your prepared dwelling place, their prayer and their supplication, and execute judgments, and be merciful to the people who have sinned against You.
verses.6:40: Now, O Lord, let Your eyes be open, I pray, and Your ears attentive to the supplication of this place.
verses.6:41: And now arise, O Lord God, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength. Let Your priests, O Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and let Your sons rejoice in good things.
verses.6:42: O Lord God, do not turn away Your face; remember the mercies of David Your servant."
verses.7:1: And when Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
verses.7:2: And the priests could not enter into the house of the Lord at that time, because the glory of the Lord had filled the house.
verses.7:3: And all the sons of Israel saw the fire coming down, and the glory of the Lord upon the house; and they fell on their faces to the ground upon the stone pavement, and worshiped and praised the Lord, saying, "For it is good, for His mercy endures forever."
verses.7:4: And the king and all the people were offering sacrifices before the Lord.
verses.7:5: And Solomon offered the sacrifice of twenty-two thousand calves; so the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
verses.7:6: And the priests were standing at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments of the songs of the Lord belonging to King David, to give thanks before the Lord, because His mercy endures forever, in the hymns of David by their hand; and the priests were sounding the trumpets before them, and all Israel was standing.
verses.7:7: And Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was in the house of the Lord; for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat.
verses.7:8: And Solomon kept the feast at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And on the eighth day he held a solemn closing assembly, for he kept the dedication of the altar as a feast for seven days.
verses.7:10: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, rejoicing and glad of heart for the good things which the Lord had done for David, for Solomon, and for Israel His people.
verses.7:11: Thus Solomon finished the house of the Lord and the house of the king; and all that Solomon had purposed in his soul to do in the house of the Lord and in his own house prospered.
verses.7:12: And God appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
verses.7:13: If I shut up heaven and there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the trees, or if I send pestilence among My people,
verses.7:14: and if My people, upon whom My name has been invoked, are humbled and pray and seek My face, and turn back from their evil ways, then I Myself will hear from heaven, and be merciful to their sins, and heal their land.
verses.7:15: Now My eyes shall be open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
verses.7:16: And now I have chosen and consecrated this house, that My name may be there forever; and My eyes and My heart shall be there all the days.
verses.7:17: And as for you, if you walk before Me as David your father did, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.7:18: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'There shall not be cut off from you a man ruling in Israel.'
verses.7:19: But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments which I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,
verses.7:20: then I will uproot you from the land which I gave to them; and this house which I have consecrated for My name I will turn away from My presence, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all the nations.
verses.7:21: And as for this lofty house, everyone who passes by it will be astonished and say, 'For what reason has the Lord done so to this land and to this house?'
verses.7:22: And they will say, 'Because they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold of other gods, and worshiped them and served them; therefore He has brought all this calamity upon them.'"
verses.8:1: And it came to pass after twenty years, during which Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own house,
verses.8:2: that the cities which Hiram had given to Solomon, Solomon built them and caused the sons of Israel to dwell there.
verses.8:3: And Solomon went to Baisoba and prevailed against it.
verses.8:4: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the fortified cities he built in Hamath.
verses.8:5: And he built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars;
verses.8:6: and Baalah, and all the fortified cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired according to his desire to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all his kingdom.
verses.8:7: All the people who were left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who are not of Israel—
verses.8:8: they were from their sons who were left with him in the land, whom the sons of Israel had utterly destroyed; and Solomon raised them to tribute until this day.
verses.8:9: But of the sons of Israel Solomon did not appoint any as servants for his kingdom; for behold, they were men of war, and rulers, and mighty men, and commanders of chariots and horsemen.
verses.8:10: And these were the chief officers of King Solomon's overseers, two hundred and fifty overseeing the labor among the people.
verses.8:11: Now Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house which he had built for her; for he said, "My wife shall not dwell in the city of David, the king of Israel, for the place is holy where the ark of the Lord has entered."
verses.8:12: Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar which he had built in front of the temple,
verses.8:13: and according to the daily requirement, to offer according to the commandments of Moses on the Sabbaths, and on the New Moons, and on the feasts, three times a year—at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.8:14: And he appointed, according to the ordinance of David, the divisions of the priests for their ministries, and the Levites over their watches to minister and to praise before the priests according to each day's requirement, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at gate after gate; for such were the commandments of David, the man of God.
verses.8:15: They did not depart from the commandments of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, or concerning the treasuries.
verses.8:16: And all the work was prepared from the day its foundation was laid until Solomon completed the house of the Lord.
verses.8:17: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Elam by the sea, in the land of Idumea.
verses.8:18: And Hiram sent by the hand of his servants ships and servants who knew the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Sophira, and took from there the four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and came to King Solomon.
verses.9:1: Now the queen of Sheba heard the name of Solomon, and she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles, with an exceedingly great retinue, and camels bearing spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones; and she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her soul.
verses.9:2: And Solomon declared to her all her matters, and not a matter escaped Solomon—not a matter which he did not declare to her.
verses.9:3: And the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built,
verses.9:4: and the food of the tables, and the seating of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers and their apparel, and his cupbearers and their attire, and the burnt offerings which he offered in the house of the Lord; and she was beside herself.
verses.9:5: And she said to the king, "True is the report which I heard in my land concerning your words and concerning your wisdom.
verses.9:6: And I did not believe the reports until I came and my eyes saw; and behold, half of the abundance of your wisdom was not declared to me—you have exceeded the report which I heard.
verses.9:7: Blessed are the men! Blessed are these your servants who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!
verses.9:8: Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you to set you upon His throne as king for the Lord your God! Because the Lord your God loved Israel, to establish them forever, therefore He has set you over them as king, to execute judgment and righteousness."
verses.9:9: And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in very great abundance, and precious stones; and there were none like those spices which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.9:10: Moreover, the servants of Solomon and the servants of Hiram brought gold to Solomon from Suphir, and pine wood, and precious stones.
verses.9:11: And the king made of the pine wood steps for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king, and lyres and harps for the singers; and nothing like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.
verses.9:12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desires, whatever she asked, besides all that she had brought to King Solomon. And she returned to her own land.
verses.9:13: Now the weight of the gold that was brought to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.9:14: besides what the subject men and the merchants brought; and all the kings of Arabia and the satraps of the land brought gold and silver to King Solomon.
verses.9:15: And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold—six hundred pieces of pure gold for one large shield, six hundred gold pieces were upon each large shield;
verses.9:16: and three hundred shields of hammered gold; and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
verses.9:17: And the king made a great throne of ivory tusks and overlaid it with refined gold.
verses.9:18: And there were six steps to the throne, bound with gold, and armrests on either side of the seat of the throne, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
verses.9:19: And twelve lions stood there upon the six steps, on the one side and on the other; nothing like it was ever made in all the kingdom.
verses.9:20: And all the vessels of King Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were overlaid with gold; silver was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
verses.9:21: For the king's ship went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram; once every three years ships came from Tarshish to the king, laden with gold, and silver, and ivory tusks, and apes.
verses.9:22: And Solomon was magnified above all the kings, both in wealth and in wisdom.
verses.9:23: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom which God had put in his heart.
verses.9:24: And each of them brought his gifts: vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments, myrrh and spices, horses and mules, year by year.
verses.9:25: And Solomon had four thousand mares for chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.9:26: And he was ruler over all the kings from the River even to the land of the foreigners, and to the borders of Egypt.
verses.9:27: And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars like the sycamores in the lowland for abundance.
verses.9:28: And the export of Solomon's horses was from Egypt and from all the earth.
verses.9:29: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Joel the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.9:30: And King Solomon reigned over all Israel forty years.
verses.9:31: And Solomon slept, and they buried him in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.
verses.10:2: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it—now he was in Egypt, since he had fled from the presence of King Solomon, and Jeroboam had dwelt in Egypt—that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
verses.10:3: And he sent and called him; and Jeroboam came, and all the assembly came to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.10:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; now therefore lighten the harsh service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he laid upon us, and we will serve you."
verses.10:5: And he said to them, "Go away for three days, and come to me." So the people departed.
verses.10:6: Then King Rehoboam assembled the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you advise me to answer a word to this people?"
verses.10:7: And they spoke to him, saying, "If today you are good to this people, and show them favor, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants all the days."
verses.10:8: But he forsook the counsel of the elders who had counseled him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
verses.10:9: And he said to them, "What do you advise that I should answer a word to this people, who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke which your father laid upon us'?"
verses.10:10: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, "Thus you shall speak to the people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, so lighten it from us'—thus you shall say, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
verses.10:11: And now my father chastised you with a heavy yoke, and I will add to our yoke; my father chastised you with whips, and I will chastise you with scorpions.'"
verses.10:12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.10:13: And the king answered harshly; and King Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders,
verses.10:14: and spoke to them according to the counsel of the younger men, saying, "My father made our yoke heavy, and I will add to it; my father chastised you with whips, and I will chastise you with scorpions."
verses.10:15: So the king did not listen to the people; for there was a turn of events from God, saying, "The Lord has established His word which He spoke by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat
verses.10:16: and all Israel, because the king did not listen to them." And the people answered the king, saying, "What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" So all Israel went to their tents.
verses.10:17: And as for the men of Israel and those who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Jeroboam reigned over them.
verses.10:18: Then Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was over the tribute, to them; and the sons of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Jeroboam hastened to mount the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.10:19: So Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day.
verses.11:1: And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, and he assembled Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand young men who waged war; and he fought against Israel to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
verses.11:2: And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.11:3: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon and to all Judah and Benjamin, saying,
verses.11:4: 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up, nor shall you fight against your brethren. Return every man to his house, for this matter has come from Me.'" And they heeded the word of the Lord, and turned back from marching against Jeroboam.
verses.11:5: And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built walled cities in Judea.
verses.11:6: He built Bethseem, and Apan, and Tekoa,
verses.11:7: and Beth-zur, and Socoh, and Adullam,
verses.11:8: and Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph,
verses.11:9: and Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,
verses.11:10: and Zorah, and Aldon, and Hebron, which belongs to Judah and Benjamin, walled cities.
verses.11:11: And he strengthened them as walled cities, and placed commanders in them, and stores of provisions, oil, and wine,
verses.11:12: in city after city shields and spears, and he made them exceedingly strong; and Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
verses.11:13: And the Levites and the priests who were in all Israel gathered to him from all the borders;
verses.11:14: for the Levites forsook the dwellings of their possession and went to Judah to Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons were casting them out from ministering to the Lord.
verses.11:15: And he appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for the idols, and for the vain things, and for the calves that Jeroboam had made.
verses.11:16: And he cast them out from the tribes of Israel, those who set their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel; and they came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.11:17: And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and strengthened Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years, for he walked in the ways of David and Solomon for three years.
verses.11:18: And Rehoboam took for himself as a wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, Baia the daughter of Elian the son of Jesse.
verses.11:19: And she bore him sons: Jaouth, Shemariah, and Roollam.
verses.11:20: And after this he took for himself Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Jethei, Ziza, and Emmoth.
verses.11:21: And Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines, for he had eighteen wives and thirty concubines; and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
verses.11:22: And he appointed Abijah the son of Maacah as chief, to be leader among his brethren, for he intended to make him king.
verses.11:23: And he was exalted above all his sons throughout all the borders of Judah and Benjamin and in the fortified cities, and he gave them a great abundance of provisions, and requested a multitude of wives.
verses.12:1: Now it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and strengthened, that he forsook the commandments of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
verses.12:2: And it happened in the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned before the Lord,
verses.12:3: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horses; and the multitude that came with him out of Egypt was without number—Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians.
verses.12:4: And they captured the fortified cities that were in Judah, and he came to Jerusalem.
verses.12:5: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the rulers of Judah who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "Thus has the Lord said: 'You have forsaken Me, and I also will forsake you into the hand of Shishak.'"
verses.12:6: And the rulers of Israel and the king were ashamed, and said, "The Lord is righteous."
verses.12:7: Now when the Lord saw that they were humbled, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, "They were humbled; I will not destroy them, and I will grant them a small measure of deliverance, and My wrath shall by no means drip upon Jerusalem,
verses.12:8: for they shall become servants, and they shall know My service and the service of the kingdom of the earth."
verses.12:9: So Shishak king of Egypt came up, and took away the treasures that were in the house of the Lord and the treasures that were in the house of the king; he took away everything. He also took away the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
verses.12:10: And Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place; and Shishak appointed over him captains of the runners, those who guarded the gate of the king.
verses.12:11: And it came to pass, whenever the king entered into the house of the Lord, that the guards and the runners went in, and those who returned to meet the runners.
verses.12:12: And when he was humbled, the wrath of the Lord turned away from him, and not to utter destruction; for indeed in Judah there were good matters.
verses.12:13: So Rehoboam grew strong in Jerusalem and reigned. Now Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of the sons of Israel to name His name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
verses.12:14: And he did evil, because he did not direct his heart to seek the Lord.
verses.12:15: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, behold, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, along with his deeds? And Rehoboam waged war against Jeroboam all the days.
verses.12:16: And Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Israel.
verses.13:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeon. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.13:3: And Abijah set the battle in array with an army of mighty warriors, four hundred thousand valiant men; and Jeroboam set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand, valiant warriors of strength.
verses.13:4: Then Abijah stood up from Mount Somoron, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear, O Jeroboam and all Israel!
verses.13:5: Is it not for you to know that the Lord God of Israel gave a king over Israel forever, to David and to his sons, by a covenant of salt?
verses.13:6: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
verses.13:7: And pestilent men, lawless sons, gathered to him, and he rose up against Rehoboam the son of Solomon; and Rehoboam was young and timid in heart, and did not withstand him.
verses.13:8: And now you say you will withstand the kingdom of the Lord, which is in the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
verses.13:9: Have you not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made for yourselves priests from the people of all the land? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with calves from the herd and seven rams becomes a priest to that which is no god.
verses.13:10: But as for us, we have not forsaken the Lord our God, and His priests minister to the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in their divisions.
verses.13:11: They burn to the Lord a burnt offering morning and evening, and compounded incense, and the rows of showbread upon the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps for burning to kindle in the evening; for we keep the charges of the Lord the God of our fathers, whereas you have forsaken Him.
verses.13:12: And behold, with us at our head is the Lord, and His priests, and the trumpets of alarm to sound the signal over us. O sons of Israel, will you fight against the Lord God of our fathers? For you shall not prosper."
verses.13:13: But Jeroboam sent an ambush around to come upon them from behind; so he was in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.
verses.13:14: And Judah turned back, and behold, the battle was against them both in front and behind; and they cried out to the Lord, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
verses.13:15: Then the men of Judah shouted; and it came to pass, as the men of Judah shouted, that the Lord struck Jeroboam and Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.13:16: And the sons of Israel fled before Judah, and the Lord delivered them into their hands.
verses.13:17: And Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, so that five hundred thousand mighty men of Israel fell slain.
verses.13:18: Thus the sons of Israel were humbled in that day, and the sons of Judah prevailed, because they hoped in the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.13:19: And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel with its villages, and Cana with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
verses.13:20: And Jeroboam did not retain strength any longer all the days of Abijah; and the Lord struck him, and he died.
verses.13:21: But Abijah grew mighty, and took for himself fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.13:22: Now the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his deeds and his words, are written in the book of the prophet Iddo.
verses.13:23: And Abijah died with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In the days of Asa the land of Judah had rest for ten years.
verses.14:1: And he did what was good and right before the Lord his God.
verses.14:2: And he removed the altars of the foreigners and the high places, and shattered the pillars, and cut down the groves,
verses.14:3: and he told Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandments.
verses.14:4: And he removed from all the cities of Judah the altars and the idols, and he had peace.
verses.14:5: There were fortified cities in the land of Judah, for the land was at peace; and he had no war in those years, because the Lord gave him rest.
verses.14:6: And he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities, and make walls and towers, gates and bars; we shall rule before the land, for just as we sought the Lord our God, He has sought us out, and has given us rest on every side, and has prospered us."
verses.14:7: And Asa had an army of armed men bearing large shields and spears in the land of Judah, three hundred thousand; and in the land of Benjamin, men bearing small shields and archers, two hundred and fifty thousand; all these were mighty men of war.
verses.14:8: And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army, with thousands and with three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Marisel.
verses.14:9: And Asa went out to meet him, and drew up for battle in the valley to the north of Mareshah.
verses.14:10: And Asa cried out to the Lord his God and said, "Lord, it is not impossible with You to save with many or with few; strengthen us, O Lord our God, for we have trusted in You, and in Your name we have come against this great multitude. O Lord our God, let no man prevail against You."
verses.14:11: And the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
verses.14:12: And Asa and his people pursued them as far as Gedor; and the Ethiopians fell so that there was no survival among them, for they were shattered before the Lord and before His army; and they carried off much spoil.
verses.14:13: And they destroyed their villages around Gedor, for terror from the Lord came upon them; and they plundered all its cities, for much spoil fell to them.
verses.14:14: And moreover they destroyed the tents of livestock, the Amazoneis, and took many sheep and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.15:1: Now the Spirit of the Lord came upon Azariah the son of Oded.
verses.15:2: And he went out to meet them in all Judah and Benjamin, and said, "The Lord is with you while we are with Him; and if you seek Him, He will be found by you; and if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
verses.15:3: And for many days Israel has been without a true God and without law.
verses.15:4: Yet He will turn them back to the Lord God of Israel, and He will be found by them.
verses.15:5: And in that time there is no peace for the one who goes in and the one who goes out, for terror from the Lord is upon all who dwell in the lands.
verses.15:6: And nation shall make war against nation and city against city, because God has terrified them with every affliction.
verses.15:7: But as for you, be strong, and do not let your hands grow weak, for there is a reward for your work."
verses.15:8: And when he heard these words and the prophecy of Adad the prophet, he took courage and cast out the abominations from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he had captured in Mount Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of the Lord that was before the temple of the Lord.
verses.15:9: And he assembled Judah and Benjamin, and the sojourners who dwelt with him from Ephraim and from Manasseh and from Simeon; for many of Israel had joined themselves to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
verses.15:10: And they were gathered together to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.15:11: And he sacrificed to the Lord on that day from what he had brought, seven hundred calves and seven thousand sheep.
verses.15:12: And he entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul,
verses.15:13: and that whoever would not seek the Lord God of Israel should die, from the youngest to the oldest, from man to woman.
verses.15:14: And they swore an oath by the Lord with a loud voice and with trumpets.
verses.15:15: And all Judah rejoiced concerning the oath, for they had sworn with all their soul, and with all their desire they sought Him, and He was found by them; and the Lord gave them rest on every side.
verses.15:16: He also removed Maachah his mother from ministering to Astarte, and he cut down the idol and burned it in the brook Kidron.
verses.15:17: Yet the high places were not removed; they still remained in Israel; nevertheless, the heart of Asa was whole all his days.
verses.15:18: And he brought in the consecrated things of David his father and the consecrated things of the house of the Lord God—silver and gold and vessels.
verses.15:19: And there was no war with him until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.16:1: And in the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah, so as to allow neither going out nor coming in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.16:2: Then Asa took gold and silver from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent to the son of Hader, king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
verses.16:3: "Make a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you gold and silver; come and drive away from me Baasha king of Israel, and let him depart from me."
verses.16:4: And the son of Hader listened to King Asa, and sent to the commanders of his army against the cities of Israel; and he struck Io, and Dano, and Abelman, and all the surrounding regions of Naphtali.
verses.16:5: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building Ramah any longer and stopped his work.
verses.16:6: Then King Asa took all Judah, and took the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had built, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.16:7: And at that time Hanami the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you have trusted in the king of Syria and have not trusted in the Lord your God, therefore the army of Syria has escaped from your hand.
verses.16:8: Were not the Ethiopians and the Libyans a great army in boldness, with horsemen in exceedingly great multitude? Yet because you trusted in the Lord, He delivered them into your hands.
verses.16:9: For the eyes of the Lord look over all the earth to strengthen every whole heart that is toward Him. You have acted without understanding in this; from now on there is war with you."
verses.16:10: And Asa was angry with the prophet, and put him in prison because of this; and Asa maltreated some of the people at that time.
verses.16:11: And behold, the acts of Asa, the first and the last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.16:12: And Asa became diseased in his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, until he was exceedingly sick; yet in his sickness he did not seek the Lord, but the physicians.
verses.16:13: And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the thirtieth year of his reign.
verses.16:14: And they buried him in the tomb that he had dug for himself in the City of David; and they laid him on the bier and filled it with spices and kinds of ointments made by perfumers, and they made for him an exceedingly great funeral.
verses.17:1: And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and Jehoshaphat strengthened himself against Israel.
verses.17:2: And he stationed forces in all the fortified cities of Judah, and appointed governors in all the cities of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had previously captured.
verses.17:3: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the former ways of his father; and he did not seek the idols,
verses.17:4: but he sought the Lord, the God of his father, and walked in the commandments of his father, and not according to the deeds of Israel.
verses.17:5: And the Lord established the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had riches and great honor.
verses.17:6: And his heart was lifted up in the way of the Lord, and he removed the high places and the groves from the land of Judah.
verses.17:7: And in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders and the sons of the mighty men—Abiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.17:8: And with them were the Levites: Samuas, Manthanias, Zebadiah, Jasiel, Shemiramoth, Jonathan, Adonijah, and Tobadobiah, who were Levites; and with them were Elishama and Joram, the priests.
verses.17:9: And they taught in Judah, and with them was the book of the law of the Lord; and they went throughout the cities of Judah and taught the people.
verses.17:10: And the dread of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the land around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.17:11: And some of the Philistines brought to Jehoshaphat gifts and silver and presents; and the Arabs brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams of the flocks.
verses.17:12: And Jehoshaphat continued to grow greater to the very heights, and he built dwellings in Judea and fortified cities.
verses.17:13: And many works were done in Judea, and men of war, mighty men of strength, were in Jerusalem.
verses.17:14: And this was their number according to their fathers' houses: of Judah, the captains of thousands—Adnah the chief, and with him three hundred thousand mighty sons of valor;
verses.17:15: and next to him was Johanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
verses.17:16: and next to him was Masaiah the son of Zari, who willingly devoted himself to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.
verses.17:17: And of Benjamin, a mighty man of valor, Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand archers and shield-bearers;
verses.17:18: and next to him was Jozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand mighty men of war.
verses.17:19: These were those who served the king, besides those whom the king placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judea.
verses.18:1: Now Jehoshaphat still had riches and honor in great abundance, and he allied himself by marriage with the house of Ahab.
verses.18:2: And after some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria; and Ahab slaughtered sheep and calves in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and treated him affectionately so that he would go up with him to Ramoth of Gilead.
verses.18:3: And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth of Gilead?" And he said to him, "As I am, so also are you; as my people are, so also are your people, with you to battle."
verses.18:4: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire today of the Lord."
verses.18:5: Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall I go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And they said, "Go up, and God will deliver it into the hands of the king."
verses.18:6: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not still a prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of him?"
verses.18:7: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man by whom we may inquire of the Lord, yet I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, for all his days are for evil; this is Micaiah the son of Jemaa." And Jehoshaphat said, "Do not let the king speak so."
verses.18:8: Then the king called a certain eunuch and said, "Bring Micaiah the son of Jemaa quickly."
verses.18:9: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, and clothed in robes; they were sitting in the open space at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.18:10: And Zedekiah the son of Canaan made for himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'With these you shall gore Syria until it is utterly destroyed.'"
verses.18:11: And all the prophets prophesied in the same way, saying, "Go up to Ramoth Gilead, and you shall prosper, and the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king."
verses.18:12: And the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Behold, the prophets have spoken good concerning the king with one mouth; please let your words be like those of one of them, and speak what is good."
verses.18:13: And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, whatever God says to me, that I will speak."
verses.18:14: So he came to the king; and the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall I go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And he said, "Go up, and you shall prosper; and they shall be delivered into your hands."
verses.18:15: And the king said to him, "How many times do I put you under oath that you speak nothing to me except the truth in the name of the Lord?"
verses.18:16: And he said, "I saw Israel scattered upon the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the Lord said, 'They have no leader; let each one return to his house in peace.'"
verses.18:17: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, but only evil?"
verses.18:18: And he said, "Not so! Hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven stood on His right hand and on His left.
verses.18:19: And the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?' And one spoke in this manner, and another spoke in that manner.
verses.18:20: Then the spirit came forward and stood before the Lord, and said, 'I will deceive him.' And the Lord said, 'By what means?'
verses.18:21: And he said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You shall deceive him, and you shall prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.18:22: Now therefore, behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
verses.18:23: Then Zedekiah the son of Canaan drew near and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said to him, "By which way did a spirit go from me—a spirit to you, the Spirit of the Lord from me—to speak to you?"
verses.18:24: And Micaiah said, "Behold, you shall see on that day; he shall enter chamber from chamber to hide himself."
verses.18:25: And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Emer the governor of the city, and to Joash the ruler, the king's son,
verses.18:26: and you shall say, 'Thus has the king said: Put this man into the prison house, and let him eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.'"
verses.18:27: And Micaiah said, "If you truly return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me; hear, all peoples!"
verses.18:28: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.18:29: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Disguise me, and I will enter into the battle, and you put on my apparel." So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
verses.18:30: Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots who were with him, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, but with the king of Israel alone."
verses.18:31: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "It is the king of Israel!" And they surrounded him to fight; but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord saved him, and God turned them away from him.
verses.18:32: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from him.
verses.18:33: And a certain man drew a bow with sure aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate; and he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand around and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
verses.18:34: And the battle turned on that day; and the king of Israel remained standing upon the chariot until evening opposite Syria, and he died as the sun was setting.
verses.19:1: And Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in Jerusalem.
verses.19:2: And Jehu the son of Hanani the prophet went out to meet him, and said to him, "O King Jehoshaphat, do you help a sinner, or show friendship to one who is hated by the Lord? Because of this, wrath from the Lord has come upon you;
verses.19:3: nevertheless, good things have been found in you, because you have removed the groves from the land of Judah, and have directed your heart to seek the Lord."
verses.19:4: And Jehoshaphat dwelt there, and again he went out among the people from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim, and brought them back to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.19:5: And he appointed judges in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.
verses.19:6: And he said to the judges, "Take heed to what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for the Lord, and with you are the matters of judgment.
verses.19:7: Now therefore, let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take care and do it, for there is no injustice with the Lord our God, nor showing of partiality, nor taking of gifts."
verses.19:8: Moreover, in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some of the priests and of the Levites and of the patriarchs of Israel for the judgment of the Lord and to judge those who dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.19:9: And he commanded them, saying, "Thus you shall act in the fear of the Lord, in truth and with a whole heart:
verses.19:10: whatever case of any man comes before you from our brethren who dwell in the midst of bloodshed, and between decree and commandment, and statutes and judgments, you shall strictly warn them, and they shall not sin against the Lord, and wrath shall not come upon you and upon your brethren. Thus you shall do, and you shall not sin.
verses.19:11: And behold, Amariah the priest is leader over you in every matter of the Lord, and Zebadiah is the leader over the house of Judah in every matter of the king; and the scribes and the Levites are before you. Be strong and act, and the Lord will be with the good."
verses.20:1: And after these things, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat to battle.
verses.20:2: And they came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea, from Syria; and behold, they are in Hasam Thamara, which is En Gedi."
verses.20:3: And Jehoshaphat was afraid, and set his face to seek the Lord, and they proclaimed a fast.
verses.20:4: And Judah gathered together to seek the Lord; indeed, from all the cities of Judah they came to seek the Lord.
verses.20:5: And Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah in Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,
verses.20:6: and said, "O Lord God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven above? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations, and in Your hand is strength of dominion, and none can withstand You.
verses.20:7: Did You not, O Lord, utterly destroy the inhabitants of this land from before Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham Your beloved forever?
verses.20:8: And they dwelt in it, and built in it a sanctuary for Your name, saying,
verses.20:9: 'If evils come upon us—sword, judgment, death, or famine—we will stand before this house and before You, for Your name is upon this house, and we will cry out to You out of affliction, and You will hear and save.'
verses.20:10: And now, behold, the sons of Ammon and Mount Seir, through whom You did not permit Israel to pass when they came out of the land of Egypt—for they turned aside from them and did not destroy them—
verses.20:11: and now, behold, they set their hand against us to come forth to cast us out from our inheritance which You gave us,
verses.20:12: O Lord our God, will You not judge among them? For we have no strength to withstand this great multitude that has come against us, and we do not know what we should do to them; rather, our eyes are upon You."
verses.20:13: And all Judah stood before the Lord, with their little children and their wives.
verses.20:14: Then upon Oziel the son of Zechariah, of the sons of Eleael the son of Manthanias, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, the Spirit of the Lord came upon him in the assembly.
verses.20:15: And he said, "Listen, all Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the Lord to you yourselves: 'Do not fear nor be dismayed before this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's.
verses.20:16: Tomorrow go down against them; behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Hasae, and you shall find them at the end of the stream of the wilderness of Jeriel.
verses.20:17: It is not for you to fight; understand these things and see the salvation of the Lord with you! Behold also Jerusalem! Do not be dismayed nor fear him; go out to meet them, and the Lord is with you.'"
verses.20:18: And Jehoshaphat bowed down upon his face, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the Lord to worship the Lord.
verses.20:19: And the Levites, of the sons of Kohath and of the sons of Korah, stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice to the heights.
verses.20:20: And they rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and cried out, "Hear me, O Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem: Trust in the Lord your God, and you shall be established; trust in His prophet, and you shall prosper."
verses.20:21: And he took counsel with the people, and appointed singers and praisers to give thanks and to praise the holy things as they went out before the army; and he said, "Give thanks to the Lord, for His mercy abides forever."
verses.20:22: And at the beginning of his praise of thanksgiving, the Lord caused the sons of Ammon to wage war against Moab and Mount Seir, who had come out against Judah, and they were routed.
verses.20:23: For the sons of Ammon and Moab turned against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly destroy and annihilate them; and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, they rose up against one another to be utterly destroyed.
verses.20:24: And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, and looked out and saw the multitude; and behold, they were all dead bodies fallen upon the earth, and no one escaped.
verses.20:25: And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, and they found much livestock, and goods, and spoils, and precious vessels, and he took spoil among them; and they were three days plundering the spoil, because it was much.
verses.20:26: And it came to pass on the fourth day that they assembled in the Valley of Blessing, for there they blessed the Lord; therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Blessing to this day.
verses.20:27: Then every man of Judah returned to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, in great gladness, for the Lord had made them rejoice over their enemies.
verses.20:28: And they entered Jerusalem with harps and with lyres and with trumpets, into the house of the Lord.
verses.20:29: And the dread of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the earth when they heard that the Lord had fought against the adversaries of Israel.
verses.20:30: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.
verses.20:31: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah; he was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.
verses.20:32: And he walked in the ways of his father Asa, and did not turn aside from doing what was upright in the sight of the Lord.
verses.20:33: Yet the high places still remained, and still the people had not directed their heart to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.20:34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the words of Joshua the son of Hanani, who wrote the book of the king of Israel.
verses.20:35: And after this Jehoshaphat allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, and he acted lawlessly
verses.20:36: in acting and going to him to build ships to go to Tarshish; and he built ships in Ezion Geber.
verses.20:37: Then Eleiada the son of Odeia, of Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have joined in friendship with Ahaziah, the Lord has broken your work, and your ships have been shattered." And he was not able to go to Tarshish.
verses.21:1: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of David; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:2: And he had six brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Mishael, and Shephatiah; all these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
verses.21:3: And their father gave them many gifts—silver, and gold, and weapons—along with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
verses.21:4: Now Jehoram arose over his kingdom and strengthened himself, and he slew all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the rulers of Israel.
verses.21:5: When he was thirty-two years old, Jehoram was established over his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.21:6: And he walked in the way of the king of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.21:7: Yet the Lord was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that He had made with David, and as He had promised him to give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.
verses.21:8: In those days Edom revolted from Judah, and set a king to reign over themselves.
verses.21:9: So Jehoram marched forth with the commanders, and all the cavalry with him; and it came to pass that he arose by night and struck Edom who surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
verses.21:10: Thus Edom revolted from Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at that time from his hand, because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.
verses.21:11: Moreover, he himself made high places in the cities of Judah, and they caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry, and he led Judah astray.
verses.21:12: And a writing came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "Thus says the Lord God of your father David: 'Because you have not walked in the way of Jehoshaphat your father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.21:13: but have walked in the ways of the king of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry just as the house of Ahab caused harlotry, and have also slain your brothers, the sons of your father, who were better than yourself,
verses.21:14: behold, the Lord will strike you with a great plague in your people, and in your sons, and in your wives, and in all your possessions;
verses.21:15: and you yourself shall be in a grievous sickness, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out by reason of the sickness from day to day.'"
verses.21:16: And the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the Philistines, and the Arabians, and those who bordered the Ethiopians;
verses.21:17: and they came up against Judah and oppressed it, and carried away all the possessions that they found in the king's house, and his sons and his daughters, so that no son was left to him except Ahaziah, the youngest of his sons.
verses.21:18: And after all these things the Lord struck him in his bowels with a sickness for which there is no cure.
verses.21:19: And it came to pass from day to day; and when the appointed time of the days came, two days, his bowels came out with the disease, and he died in a grievous sickness. And his people did not make a funeral for him like the funeral of his fathers.
verses.21:20: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem; and he departed without praise, and was buried in the City of David, yet not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.22:1: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the band of raiders that had come upon them—the Arabians, the Alimazoneans—had slain all the older ones. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
verses.22:2: Ahaziah was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.
verses.22:3: He also walked in the way of the house of Ahab, for his mother was a counselor to sin.
verses.22:4: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, like the house of Ahab; for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to destroy him.
verses.22:5: And he walked in their counsels, and went with Joram the son of Ahab to battle against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead; and the archers struck Joram.
verses.22:6: And Joram returned to Israel to be healed of the wounds with which the Syrians had struck him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Israel, because he was sick.
verses.22:7: And from God came the downfall of Ahaziah by his coming to Joram; and when he went out, Joram went out with him to the son of Nimshi, the anointed of the Lord concerning the house of Ahab.
verses.22:8: And it came to pass, as Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, that they found the rulers of Judah and the brothers of Ahaziah who ministered to Ahaziah, and he slew them.
verses.22:9: And he commanded to seek Ahaziah; and they seized him while he was being healed in Samaria, and brought him to Jehu, and he slew him. And they buried him, for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart." And there was no one in the house of Ahaziah to maintain power for the kingdom.
verses.22:10: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed of the kingdom in the house of Judah.
verses.22:11: But Jehoshabeath took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from the midst of the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the sister of Ahaziah and wife of Jehoiada, hid him; she hid him from the face of Athaliah, so that she did not slay him.
verses.22:12: And he was hidden with him in the house of God six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.23:1: And in the eighth year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the captains of hundreds—Azariah the son of Joram, Ishmael the son of Johanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Azeiah, and Elishaphan the son of Zechariah—with him into the house.
verses.23:2: And they went around Judah, and he gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.23:3: And all the assembly of Judah made a covenant in the house of God with the king. And he showed them the king's son and said to them, "Behold, let the king's son reign, just as the Lord spoke concerning the house of David.
verses.23:4: Now this is the thing which you shall do: a third of you, of the priests and of the Levites, shall enter on the Sabbath, even to the gates of the entrances,
verses.23:5: and a third shall be at the king's house, and a third at the middle gate; and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.23:6: And let no one enter the house of the Lord except the priests and the Levites and those of the Levites who minister; they shall enter, for they are holy; and let all the people keep the watches for the Lord.
verses.23:7: And the Levites shall surround the king all around, every man with his weapon in his hand; and whoever enters into the house shall die. And they shall be with the king as he goes in and as he goes out."
