verses.23:8: And the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And each man took his men from the beginning of the Sabbath until the close of the Sabbath, for Jehoiada did not dismiss the divisions.
verses.23:9: And he gave the swords and the large shields and the weapons that belonged to King David in the house of God.
verses.23:10: And he stationed all the people, each man with his weapons, from the right side of the house to the left side of the altar and of the house, all around the king.
verses.23:11: And he brought out the king's son, and put upon him the royal crown and the testimonies; and Jehoiada and his sons made him king and anointed him, and said, "Long live the king!"
verses.23:12: And Athaliah heard the voice of the people running and giving thanks and praising the king, and she entered to the king in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:13: And she looked, and behold, the king was at his station, and at the entrance were the rulers and the trumpets, rulers around the king; and all the people rejoiced and blew the trumpets, and those singing with the instruments, singers and those chanting praise. And Athaliah tore her robe and cried out, "Conspiring, you conspire!"
verses.23:14: And Jehoiada the priest went out; and Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds and the commanders of the army, and said to them, "Cast her outside the house, and go in after her, and let her die by the sword." For the priest said, "Do not let her die in the house of the Lord."
verses.23:15: And they made way for her, and she passed through the gate of the horsemen of the king's house, and they put her to death there.
verses.23:16: And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and the people and the king, that they should be a people for the Lord.
verses.23:17: And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down, together with his altars and his idols, and ground them to dust; and they put Mattan the priest of Baal to death before his altars.
verses.23:18: And Jehoiada the priest entrusted the works of the house of the Lord to the hand of the priests and Levites, and he established the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, which David had appointed over the house of the Lord, and to offer up burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the Law of Moses, with gladness and with songs, by the hand of David.
verses.23:19: And the gatekeepers stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, and no one unclean in any matter would enter.
verses.23:20: And he took the heads of the fathers' houses and the mighty men and the rulers of the people and all the people of the land, and they brought the king up into the house of the Lord; and he entered through the inner gate into the king's house, and they seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.23:21: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they had put Athaliah to death.
verses.24:1: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abia from Beersheba.
verses.24:2: And Joash did what was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.24:3: And Jehoiada took for himself two wives, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.24:4: And it came to pass after these things that it came into the heart of Joash to repair the house of the Lord.
verses.24:5: And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah, and gather silver from all Israel to strengthen the house of the Lord year by year, and make haste to speak." Yet the Levites did not believe.
verses.24:6: And King Joash called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not inquired concerning the Levites, to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem what was decreed by Moses the man of God, because he assembled Israel to the tabernacle of the testimony?"
verses.24:7: For Athaliah was that lawless woman, and her sons tore down the house of God, and indeed they used the holy things of the house of the Lord for the Baals.
verses.24:8: And the king said, "Let a chest be made and placed outside at the gate of the house of the Lord,
verses.24:9: and let them proclaim in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to the Lord, just as Moses the servant of God spoke concerning Israel in the wilderness."
verses.24:10: And all the rulers and all the people gave, and they brought in and cast into the chest until it was filled.
verses.24:11: And it came to pass, when they brought the chest to the king's overseers by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that the silver had become plentiful, the king's scribe and the overseer of the high priest came and emptied the chest, and restored it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and gathered much silver.
verses.24:12: And the king and Jehoiada the priest gave it to those who did the work for the service of the house of the Lord; and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord, and smiths of iron and bronze to repair the house of the Lord.
verses.24:13: And those who did the works labored, and the length of the works went up in their hands; and they raised up the house of the Lord to its proper state and strengthened it.
verses.24:14: And when they had finished, they brought the remainder of the silver to the king and to Jehoiada, and they made vessels for the house of the Lord, vessels of ministry for burnt offerings, and censers of gold and silver. And they offered up burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.24:15: And Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died; he was one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
verses.24:16: And they buried him in the City of David among the kings, because he had done good with Israel, and with God and His house.
verses.24:17: And it came to pass after the death of Jehoiada that the rulers of Judah came in and bowed down to the king; then the king listened to them.
verses.24:18: And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, and served the Astartes and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem on that day.
verses.24:19: And He sent prophets to them to turn them back to the Lord, and they did not listen; and they testified against them, and they did not obey.
verses.24:20: And the Spirit of God clothed Azariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Why do you transgress the commandments of the Lord? And you shall not prosper; because you have forsaken the Lord, He will also forsake you.'"
verses.24:21: And they conspired against him, and stoned him at the command of Joash the king in the court of the house of the Lord.
verses.24:22: And Joash did not remember the mercy which Jehoiada his father had shown to him, and he put his son to death. And as he was dying, he said, "May the Lord see and judge!"
verses.24:23: And it came to pass after the end of the year that the army of Syria came up against him, and came against Judah and against Jerusalem; and they destroyed all the rulers of the people among the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.
verses.24:24: For the army of Syria came with a few men, yet God delivered a very great army into their hands, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. And with Joash He executed judgments.
verses.24:25: And after they departed from him, when they left him in great infirmities, his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and put him to death on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the tomb of the kings.
verses.24:26: And those who conspired against him were Zabel the son of Sama the Ammonite, and Zozabed the son of Somaioth the Moabite,
verses.24:27: and all his sons, and the five came to him. And the rest, behold, they are written in the record of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.25:1: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jonaa of Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, yet not with a full heart.
verses.25:3: Now it came to pass, when the kingdom was established in his hand, that he put to death his servants who had murdered the king his father.
verses.25:4: Yet their sons he did not slay, according to the covenant of the law of the Lord as it is written, as the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for children, nor shall sons die for fathers, but each one shall die for his own sin."
verses.25:5: Then Amaziah gathered the house of Judah together and appointed them according to their fathers' houses, under captains of thousands and captains of hundreds throughout all Judah and Jerusalem; and he numbered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand, mighty men able to go forth to war, holding spear and shield.
verses.25:6: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty men of valor for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.25:7: And a man of God came to him, saying, "O king, the army of Israel shall not go with you, for the Lord is not with Israel, with all the sons of Ephraim.
verses.25:8: For if you suppose to prevail by these, then the Lord will put you to flight before the enemies; for it is from the Lord both to prevail and to put to flight."
verses.25:9: And Amaziah said to the man of God, "And what shall I do about the hundred talents which I gave to the army of Israel?" And the man of God said, "The Lord is able to give you far more than these."
verses.25:10: So Amaziah separated the army that had come to him from Ephraim, to depart to their own place; and they grew exceedingly angry against Judah, and returned to their own place in fierce wrath.
verses.25:11: And Amaziah strengthened himself and took his people, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down there ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
verses.25:12: And ten thousand the sons of Judah captured alive, and brought them to the top of the cliff, and cast them down from the top of the cliff, so that they were all dashed to pieces.
verses.25:13: But the men of the army whom Amaziah had sent back so that they would not be found with him in battle fell upon the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth Horon, and struck down three thousand among them and carried off great spoil.
verses.25:14: Now it came to pass, after Amaziah returned from striking down Idumea, that he brought to them the gods of the sons of Seir, and set them up as gods for himself, and stood before them to worship, and himself sacrificed to them.
verses.25:15: Therefore the wrath of the Lord came upon Amaziah, and He sent prophets to him, and they said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people, which did not deliver their own people from your hand?"
verses.25:16: And it came to pass, as he spoke to him, that he said to him, "Have I appointed you counselor to the king? Take heed, lest you be scourged." Then the prophet kept silent, and said, "I know that He has purposed against you to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
verses.25:18: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And behold, the wild beasts of the field that are in Lebanon shall come; and the wild beasts came and trampled down the thistle.
verses.25:19: You have said, 'Behold, you have struck down Idumea,' and your heavy heart lifts you up. Now stay in your house; and why do you meddle in evil, so that you shall fall, you and Judah with you?"
verses.25:20: But Amaziah did not listen, for it came from the Lord, to deliver him into their hands, because he had sought the gods of the Idumeans.
verses.25:21: So Joash king of Israel went up, and they faced one another, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.25:22: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his tent.
verses.25:23: Then Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, at Beth Shemesh, and brought them to Jerusalem, and broke down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.
verses.25:24: And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord and with Obed-Edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.25:25: And Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash the son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.25:26: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, behold, are they not written in the book of Judah and Israel?
verses.25:27: And from the time that Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they formed a conspiracy against him, and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.25:28: And they brought him back upon horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of David.
verses.26:1: Then all the people of the land took Ahaziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.26:2: He built Elath; he restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.26:3: Uzziah was sixteen years old, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Chaia of Jerusalem.
verses.26:4: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
verses.26:5: And he sought the Lord throughout all the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the fear of the Lord; and in his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord prospered him.
verses.26:6: And he went forth and made war against the Philistines, and broke down the walls of Gath and the walls of Abner and the walls of Ashdod, and built cities of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
verses.26:7: And the Lord strengthened him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who dwelt upon the rock, and against the Meunites.
verses.26:8: And the Meunites gave gifts to Uzziah, and his name reached even to the entrance of Egypt, for he grew exceedingly strong.
verses.26:9: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem both at the Corner Gate and at the gate of the corner of the valley and at the corners, and fortified them.
verses.26:10: He also built towers in the wilderness and hewed out many cisterns, for he had much livestock both in the Shephelah and in the plain, and vinedressers in the hill country and on Carmel, for he was a husbandman.
verses.26:11: And Uzziah had armies that made war and went forth to battle array by number; and their numbering was by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Amasai the judge, under the hand of Hananiah the king's deputy.
verses.26:12: The entire number of the chief fathers among the mighty men of war was two thousand six hundred.
verses.26:13: And with them was a fighting army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred; these were the ones who made war with mighty power to help the king against the adversaries.
verses.26:14: And Uzziah prepared for them, for all the army, shields and spears and helmets and breastplates and bows and slings for stones.
verses.26:15: And he made in Jerusalem engines devised by a skillful designer, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones; and their construction was heard of far abroad, for he was marvelously helped until he became strong.
verses.26:16: But when he became strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction; and he transgressed against the Lord his God, and entered into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: So Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, valiant men.
verses.26:18: And they withstood King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to offer sacrifice to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to offer sacrifice. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have departed from the Lord; and this shall not be for your glory from the Lord God."
verses.26:19: Then Uzziah became furious, and in his hand was the censer to burn incense in the temple; and while he was furious with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, and above the altar of incense.
verses.26:20: And the chief priest and the priests turned toward him, and behold, he was leprous on his forehead; and they hurried him out from there, and indeed he himself hastened to go out, because the Lord had rebuked him.
verses.26:21: And King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house as a leper, because he was cut off from the house of the Lord; and Jotham his son was over his kingdom, judging the people of the land.
verses.26:22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, are written by Jesse the prophet.
verses.26:23: So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial of the kings, for they said, "He is a leper." Then Jotham his son reigned in his place.
verses.27:1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jerusha, the daughter of Sador.
verses.27:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not enter into the temple of the Lord; yet the people still acted corruptly.
verses.27:3: He built the High Gate of the house of the Lord, and on his wall of Ophel he built much;
verses.27:4: in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests both dwellings and towers.
verses.27:5: He also fought against the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed against him. And they gave him each year one hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley; these the king of Ammon brought to him each year, in the first year and the second and the third.
verses.27:6: So Jotham grew mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.
verses.27:7: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and his war and his deeds, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.27:9: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of David; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.28:1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the sight of the Lord, like David his father.
verses.28:2: And he walked according to the ways of the king of Israel; for he also made carved images among their idols.
verses.28:3: He offered sacrifice in Gaibenthom and caused his children to pass through the fire, along with the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.28:4: And he burned incense upon the high places and upon the housetops and beneath every leafy tree.
verses.28:5: And the Lord his God delivered him by the hand of the kings of Syria, and struck against him, and they carried away from them a great multitude of captives; for He also delivered him into the hands of the kings of Israel, and struck him with a great blow.
verses.28:6: And Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, sent into Judah in one day one hundred and twenty thousand men mighty in strength, because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.28:7: And Zichri, the mighty man of Ephraim, slew Maaseiah the king's son, and Egdreikan the commander of his house, and Elkanah the king's successor.
verses.28:8: And the sons of Israel took captive from their brethren three hundred thousand—women, sons, and daughters—and they plundered much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Samaria.
verses.28:9: And there was the prophet of the Lord there, Oded by name; and he went out to meet the army of those coming to Samaria, and said to them, "Behold, the wrath of the Lord, the God of your fathers, was upon Judah, and He delivered them into your hands, and you have slain among them in wrath; it has reached even to the heavens.
verses.28:10: And now you propose to acquire the sons of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female servants; behold, is it not for you, with yourselves, to bear witness to the Lord our God?
verses.28:11: And now hear me, and send back the captives whom you have taken captive of your brethren, for the wrath of the Lord is upon you."
verses.28:12: And leaders from the sons of Ephraim rose up—Oudeia the son of Johanan, and Zechariah the son of Meshillemoth, and Hezekiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Choad—against those who were coming from the war.
verses.28:13: And they said to them, "You shall by no means bring the captives here to us, for you propose to bring sin against the Lord upon us, to add to our sins and to our ignorance; for our sin is great, and the wrath of the Lord God is upon Israel."
verses.28:14: So the warriors left the captives and the spoil before the leaders and all the assembly.
verses.28:15: And the men who were designated by name rose up and took charge of the captives, and from the spoil they covered all who were naked, and clothed them and put sandals on them, and gave them to eat and to anoint themselves; and they also assisted every feeble one with beasts of burden, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren, and returned to Samaria.
verses.28:16: At that time Ahaz sent to the king of Assyria to help him,
verses.28:17: and in this matter also, because the Edomites had attacked and struck Judah and carried away captives.
verses.28:18: And the Philistines also raided the cities of the lowland and the south of Judah, and took Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Galero, and Soco with its villages, and Galezo with its villages; and they dwelt there.
verses.28:19: For the Lord humbled Judah on account of Ahaz king of Judah, because he had departed in apostasy from the Lord.
verses.28:20: And Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came against him, and they afflicted him.
verses.28:21: And Ahaz took the things in the house of the Lord and the things in the house of the king and of the leaders, and gave them to the king of Assyria; yet it was not for their help,
verses.28:22: but rather for his own affliction. And he continued yet more to depart from the Lord; and the king said,
verses.28:23: "I will seek out the gods of Damascus who strike me." And he said, "The gods of the king of Syria—they will strengthen them; therefore I will sacrifice to them, and they will help me." And they became a stumbling block to him and to all Israel.
verses.28:24: And Ahaz removed the vessels of the house of the Lord and cut them in pieces, and shut the doors of the house of the Lord, and made for himself altars in every corner,
verses.28:25: and in every single city in Judah he made high places to burn incense to foreign gods; and they provoked to anger the Lord, the God of their fathers.
verses.28:26: Now the rest of his words and his deeds, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.28:27: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David, because they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:1: And Hezekiah became king at twenty-five years of age, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abba, the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.29:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.29:3: And it came to pass, when he was established over his kingdom, in the first month, that he opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.
verses.29:4: And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and stationed them on the side toward the east,
verses.29:5: and said to them, "Hear, O Levites! Now purify yourselves, and purify the house of the Lord, the God of your fathers, and cast out the uncleanness from the holy places.
verses.29:6: For our fathers have departed and done what is evil before the Lord, and have forsaken Him, and have turned away their face from the tabernacle of the Lord and turned their backs;
verses.29:7: and they shut up the doors of the temple, and extinguished the lamps, and did not burn incense, and did not offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
verses.29:8: And the Lord was angry with wrath against Judah and Jerusalem, and He delivered them over to astonishment and to hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
verses.29:9: And behold, your fathers have been struck down by the sword, and your sons and your daughters and your wives are in captivity in a land not their own, which is so even now.
verses.29:10: Because of these things it is now in my heart to make my covenant, a covenant of the Lord, the God of Israel; and He has turned away the wrath of His anger from us.
verses.29:11: And now do not be negligent, for He has chosen you to stand before Him to minister, and to be His ministers and to burn incense."
verses.29:12: And the Levites rose up: Mahath the son of Masi and Joel the son of Zechariah, of the sons of Kohath; and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi and Zechariah the son of Elle; and of the sons of Gershon, those from Zemmath and Jodan—these were sons of Joah;
verses.29:13: and of the sons of Elizaphan, both Zambri and Jeiel; and of the sons of Asa, Azariah and Mattaniah;
verses.29:14: and of the sons belonging to Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.29:15: And he gathered their brethren, and they purified themselves according to the command of the king by the decree of the Lord.
verses.29:16: And the priests went even into the house of the Lord to purify it, and cast out all the uncleanness that was found in the house of the Lord, even into the court of the house of the Lord; and the Levites received it to cast it out into the brook Kidron.
verses.29:17: And they began to purify on the third day, the new moon of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they entered into the temple of the Lord; and they purified the house of the Lord in eight days, and on the thirteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.29:18: And they went inside to Hezekiah the king and said, "We have purified all the things in the house of the Lord, the altar of burnt offering and its vessels, and the table of the showbread and its vessels,
verses.29:19: and all the vessels which Ahaz the king defiled in his reign in his apostasy we have prepared and purified; behold, they are before the altar of the Lord."
verses.29:20: And Hezekiah the king rose up early and gathered the leaders of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord.
verses.29:21: And he brought up seven young bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering, for the kingdom and for the holy places and for Israel; and he spoke to the sons of Aaron, the priests, to go up to the altar of the Lord.
verses.29:22: And they slaughtered the young bulls, and the priests received the blood and poured it upon the altar; and they slaughtered the rams, and poured the blood upon the altar.
verses.29:23: And they brought near the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.
verses.29:24: And the priests slaughtered them, and made atonement with their blood at the altar, and made atonement for all Israel; for "For all Israel," said the king, "are the burnt offering and the sin offerings."
verses.29:25: And he stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, with harps, and with lyres, according to the command of David the king, and of Gad the prophet, and of Nathan the prophet; for the decree was by the command of the Lord through the hand of the prophets.
verses.29:26: And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.29:27: And Hezekiah commanded to offer up the burnt offering upon the altar; and when they began to offer up the burnt offering, they began to sing to the Lord, and the trumpets sounded with the instruments of David the king.
verses.29:28: And the entire assembly worshiped, and the singers were singing and the trumpets were sounding until the burnt offering was finished.
verses.29:29: And when they had finished offering, the king and all who were present bowed down and worshiped.
verses.29:30: And Hezekiah the king and the leaders told the Levites to sing praise to the Lord with the words of David and of Asaph the prophet; and they sang praise with gladness, and fell down and worshiped.
verses.29:31: And Hezekiah answered and said, "Now you have filled your hands to the Lord; draw near and bring sacrifices and offerings of praise into the house of the Lord." And the assembly brought sacrifices and offerings of praise into the house of the Lord, and everyone who was willing in heart brought burnt offerings.
verses.29:32: And the number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was seventy young bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.29:33: And the consecrated offerings were six hundred young bulls and three thousand five hundred sheep.
verses.29:34: However, the priests were too few and were not able to skin the burnt offering; so their brethren the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had purified themselves, for the Levites purified themselves more eagerly than the priests.
verses.29:35: And the burnt offering was abundant, with the fat portions of the consecration of the peace offering and the drink offerings of the burnt offering; and the work in the house of the Lord was set in order.
verses.29:36: And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because God had made preparation for the people, for the matter had come about suddenly.
verses.30:1: And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.30:2: And the king and the rulers and all the assembly that was in Jerusalem took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month.
verses.30:3: For they were not able to keep it at that time, because the priests had not consecrated themselves in sufficient number, and the people had not been gathered to Jerusalem.
verses.30:4: And the matter was pleasing in the sight of the king and in the sight of the assembly.
verses.30:5: So they established a decree to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel at Jerusalem, for a multitude had not kept it according to what was written.
verses.30:6: And the runners went with the letters from the king and the rulers throughout all Israel and Judah, according to the command of the king, saying, "O children of Israel, return to the God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, and bring back those who have escaped, who are left from the hand of the king of Assyria.
verses.30:7: And do not be like your fathers and your brethren, who departed from the Lord God of their fathers, and He gave them over to desolation, as you see.
verses.30:8: And now do not harden your hearts; give glory to the Lord God, and enter into His sanctuary, which He has sanctified forever, and serve the Lord your God, and He will turn away from you the fierceness of wrath.
verses.30:9: For when you return to the Lord, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before all who took them captive, and He will bring them back to this land; for the Lord our God is merciful and compassionate, and He will not turn His face away from you, if we return to Him."
verses.30:10: And the runners passed from city to city in the hill country of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun; yet they were as ones laughing at them and mocking them.
verses.30:11: Nevertheless, men of Asher and from Manasseh and from Zebulun turned, and came to Jerusalem and into Judah.
verses.30:12: And the hand of the Lord was there to give them one heart to come and act according to the commands of the king and the rulers, by the word of the Lord.
verses.30:13: And many people gathered to Jerusalem to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, an exceedingly great assembly.
verses.30:14: And they arose and tore down the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the things on which they had burned incense to the false gods they pulled down and cast into the Brook Kidron.
verses.30:15: And they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month; and the priests and the Levites were put to shame and consecrated themselves, and brought burnt offerings into the house of the Lord.
verses.30:16: And they stood at their post according to their ordinance, according to the commandment of Moses the man of God; and the priests received the blood from the hand of the Levites.
verses.30:17: For a multitude of the assembly had not consecrated themselves; therefore the Levites were in charge of slaughtering the Passover for everyone who was not able to be consecrated to the Lord.
verses.30:18: For a great part of the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not consecrated themselves, yet they ate this Passover contrary to what was written. And Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the good Lord make atonement
verses.30:19: for every heart that sets itself aright to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, though not according to the purification of the holy things."
verses.30:20: And the Lord listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
verses.30:21: And the children of Israel who were found in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great gladness, singing praises to the Lord day by day, both the priests and the Levites with instruments to the Lord.
verses.30:22: And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites and of those who had good understanding for the Lord; and they completed the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days, offering sacrifices of deliverance and giving thanks to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.30:23: And the assembly took counsel together to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days with gladness.
verses.30:24: For Hezekiah gave as an offering to Judah, to the assembly, one thousand calves and seven thousand sheep; and the rulers gave as an offering to the people one thousand calves and ten thousand sheep; and the consecrated offerings of the priests were in great abundance.
verses.30:25: And all the assembly rejoiced—the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly of Judah, and those who were found from Israel, and the sojourners who came from the land of Israel, and those who dwelt in Judah.
verses.30:26: And there was great gladness in Jerusalem; since the days of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, there had not been such a feast in Jerusalem.
verses.30:27: And the priests, the Levites, arose and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to His holy dwelling place, to heaven.
verses.31:1: And when all these things were finished, all Israel who were found in the cities of Judah went out, and shattered the pillars, and cut down the sacred groves, and tore down the high places and the altars from all the land of Judea and Benjamin and Ephraim and from Manasseh, to the very end; and all Israel returned, each man to his inheritance and to their cities.
verses.31:2: And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and the divisions of each man according to his own ministry, for the priests and for the Levites, for the burnt offering and for the sacrifice of deliverance, and to praise and to give thanks and to minister in the gates in the courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.31:3: And the king's portion from his own possessions was for the burnt offerings—the morning and the evening—and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the feasts that are written in the law of the Lord.
verses.31:4: And they told the people who dwelt in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be strengthened in the ministry of the house of the Lord.
verses.31:5: And as he commanded the word, Israel gave in abundance the firstfruits of grain and wine and oil and honey, and all the produce of the field; and the children of Israel and Judah brought all the tithes in great abundance.
verses.31:6: And those who dwelt in the cities of Judah, they also brought tithes of calves and sheep, and tithes of goats, and consecrated them to the Lord their God, and brought them in and laid them in heaps.
verses.31:7: In the third month the foundation heaps began to be laid, and in the seventh month they were finished.
verses.31:8: And Hezekiah and the rulers came and saw the heaps, and they blessed the Lord and His people Israel.
verses.31:9: And Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.
verses.31:10: And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, spoke and said, "Since the firstfruits began to be brought into the house of the Lord, we have eaten and drunk and left over; for the Lord has blessed His people, and we have left over to this great abundance."
verses.31:11: And Hezekiah gave word to prepare chambers in the house of the Lord; and they prepared them.
verses.31:12: And they brought there the firstfruits and the tithes faithfully; and over them as overseer was Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second in charge,
verses.31:13: and Jehiel, Uzziah, Maeth, Asahel, Jerimoth, Ezabath, Jeiel, Samachiah, Thanai, and Benaiah and his sons were appointed under Conaniah and Shimei his brother, as King Hezekiah and Azariah the ruler of the house of the Lord had commanded.
verses.31:14: And Kore the son of Heman the Levite, the gatekeeper toward the east, was over the gifts, to distribute the firstfruits to the Lord and the most holy things.
verses.31:15: By the hand of Odom, Benjamin, Jeshua, Shimei, Marias, and Shecaniah, through the hand of the priests, they were faithfully to distribute to their brethren according to the divisions, both to the great and to the small—
verses.31:16: each one of the male offspring from three years old and upward, to everyone who entered the house of the Lord, for their daily portion day by day, for the ministry in the divisions of their order.
verses.31:17: This was the enrollment of the priests according to their fathers' houses, and the Levites in their divisions from twenty years old and upward, in their order,
verses.31:18: to enroll them with all the offspring of their sons and their daughters, for the whole multitude; for in faithfulness they consecrated the holy thing.
verses.31:19: And for the sons of Aaron who served as priests, and those from their cities, in every city there were men who were designated by name to give a portion to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.
verses.31:20: And thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah, and he did what was good and right in the sight of the Lord his God.
verses.31:21: And in every work that he began in the service of the house of the Lord, and in the law and in the commandments, he sought his God with all his soul; and he acted and prospered.
verses.32:1: And after these matters and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came, and he came against Judah and encamped against the walled cities, and purposed to seize them.
verses.32:2: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem.
verses.32:3: And he took counsel with his elders and the mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that were outside the city, and they joined to strengthen him.
verses.32:4: And he gathered many people and stopped up the waters of the springs and the river that runs through the city, saying, "Lest the king of Assyria come and find much water and prevail."
verses.32:5: And Hezekiah strengthened himself and rebuilt all the wall that had been broken down, and towers, and another outer wall outside, and he strengthened the bastion of the city of David, and prepared many weapons.
verses.32:6: And he appointed captains of war over the people, and they were gathered to him in the open square of the Valley Gate, and he spoke to their heart, saying,
verses.32:7: "Be strong and act courageously; do not be terrified before the king of Assyria, nor before all the nation that is with him, for there are more with us than with him.
verses.32:8: With him are arms of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God, to save and to fight our battle." And the people took courage at the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.32:9: And after this Sennacherib king of the Assyrians sent his servants to Jerusalem—while he himself was against Lachish, and all the host with him—and he sent to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
verses.32:10: "Thus says the king of the Assyrians: In what do you trust? Will you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.32:11: Does Hezekiah not deceive you, to deliver you over to death and to famine and to thirst, saying, 'The Lord our God will save you from the hand of the king of Assyria'?
verses.32:12: This is Hezekiah who removed His altars and His high places, and spoke to Judah and to those who dwell in Jerusalem, saying, 'Before this altar you shall worship, and upon it you shall burn incense.'
verses.32:13: Do you not know what I and my fathers did to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of all the earth at all able to save their people from my hand?
verses.32:14: Who among all the gods of these nations whom my fathers utterly destroyed? Were they able to save their people from my hand, that your God should be able to save you from my hand?
verses.32:15: Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him cause you to trust in this manner, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation and kingdom shall by any means be able to save his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers; for your God shall by no means save you from my hand."
verses.32:16: And his servants spoke still further against the Lord God and against Hezekiah His servant.
verses.32:17: And he wrote a letter to reproach the Lord God of Israel, and spoke concerning Him, saying, "Just as the gods of the nations of the earth did not deliver their peoples from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah shall by no means deliver His people from my hand."
verses.32:18: And he cried out with a loud voice in the Judean tongue to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to help them and to pull down, in order that they might seize the city.
verses.32:19: And he spoke against the God of Jerusalem even as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the works of the hands of men.
verses.32:20: And Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed concerning these things and cried out to heaven.
verses.32:21: And the Lord sent an angel; he wiped out every mighty man and warrior and leader and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he returned with shame of face to his own land. And he went into the house of his god, and some of those who had come forth from his own body struck him down with the sword.
verses.32:22: And the Lord saved Hezekiah and those who dwelt in Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all, and He gave them rest on every side.
verses.32:23: And many brought gifts to the Lord to Jerusalem and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was greatly exalted in the sight of all the nations after these things.
verses.32:24: In those days Hezekiah fell sick even to death, and he prayed to the Lord; and He heard him and gave him a sign.
verses.32:25: And Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit that He had given him, but his heart was lifted up; and wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.32:26: And Hezekiah humbled himself from the loftiness of his heart, both he and those who dwelt in Jerusalem, and the wrath of God did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
verses.32:27: And Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and glory; and he made for himself treasuries for silver and gold and precious stones, and for spices, and armories, and for desirable vessels,
verses.32:28: and cities for the produce of grain and oil and wine, and stalls for every kind of livestock, and folds for the flocks,
verses.32:29: and cities which he built for himself, and possessions of sheep and cattle in abundance, for the Lord gave him exceedingly great possessions.
verses.32:30: Hezekiah himself stopped up the upper outlet of the water of Zion, and directed them straight down to the west of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.
verses.32:31: And thus, concerning the envoys of the rulers from Babylon who were sent to him to inquire of him about the wonder that had taken place in the land, the Lord forsook him to test him, to know the things that were in his heart.
verses.32:32: And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his mercy, behold, they are written in the prophecy of Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.32:33: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and those who dwelt in Jerusalem gave him glory and honor at his death. And Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, after all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:3: And he returned and built the high places which Hezekiah his father had torn down, and he set up pillars for the Baals and made sacred groves, and he worshiped all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.33:4: And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said, "In Jerusalem My name shall be forever."
verses.33:5: And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.33:6: And he himself caused his children to pass through fire in Ge-Bane-Hinnom; and he practiced soothsaying and sorcery and augury, and he appointed mediums and enchanters; he multiplied doing evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.33:7: And he set the carved and molten image, the likeness which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.
verses.33:8: And I will not again dislodge the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, only if they take care to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law, the statutes, and the judgments by the hand of Moses."
verses.33:9: And Manasseh led Judah and those who dwelt in Jerusalem astray, to do evil more than all the nations whom the Lord had removed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:10: And the Lord spoke against Manasseh and against his people, and he did not listen.
verses.33:11: And the Lord brought upon them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, and they seized Manasseh in bonds and bound him in fetters and led him to Babylon.
verses.33:12: And when he was afflicted, he sought the face of the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers;
verses.33:13: and he prayed to Him, and He heard him; and He heard his cry, and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that the Lord, He is God.
verses.33:14: And after these things he built a wall outside the city of David on the west along Gihon in the valley, and at the exit of the gate round about, and even to Ophel itself, and he raised it exceedingly high; and he appointed captains of the army in all the walled cities in Judah.
verses.33:15: And he removed the foreign gods and the carved image from the house of the Lord, and all the altars which he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem and outside the city.
verses.33:16: And he restored the altar of the Lord, and sacrificed upon it a sacrifice of deliverance and praise, and he told Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.
verses.33:17: Nevertheless, the people were still on the high places; yet the Lord was their God.
verses.33:18: And the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the God of Israel,
verses.33:19: behold, they are in the words of his prayer, and He heard him; and all his sins and his apostasies, and the places upon which he built the high places and set up sacred groves and carved images there before he turned back, behold, they are written in the words of the seers.
verses.33:20: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the garden of his house; and Amos his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:21: Amos was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:22: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done; and to all the idols which Manasseh his father had made, Amos sacrificed and served them.
verses.33:23: And he did not humble himself before the Lord as Manasseh his father had humbled himself, for his son Amos multiplied trespass.
verses.33:24: And his servants set upon him and struck him down in his house.
verses.33:25: And the people of the land struck down those who had set upon King Amos; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.34:1: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
verses.34:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.34:3: And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the Lord, the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the groves, and from the cast images.
verses.34:4: And he tore down before his face the altars of the Baals and the high places that were above them; and he cut down the groves and the carved images, and the cast images he broke in pieces and ground to dust, and cast upon the face of the graves of those who sacrificed to them.
verses.34:5: And he burned the bones of the priests upon the altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.34:6: and in the cities of Ephraim and Manasseh and Simeon and Naphtali, and in their places round about.
verses.34:7: And he tore down the groves and the altars, and cut the idols into fine pieces, and cut down all the high places throughout all the land of Israel; and he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:8: Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Selia, and Maasa the ruler of the city, and Joah the son of Joach his recorder, to repair the house of the Lord his God.
verses.34:9: And they came to Hilkiah the high priest and delivered the silver that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the gate had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of the rulers, and from all the remnant in Israel, and of the sons of Judah and Benjamin, and of those who dwelt in Jerusalem.
verses.34:10: And they put it into the hand of the workmen who were appointed in the house of the Lord, and they gave it to the workmen who were working in the house of the Lord, to mend and strengthen the house.
verses.34:11: And they gave it to the carpenters and to the builders, to buy squared stones and timber for beams to roof the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.
verses.34:12: And the men were faithful in the work; and over them as overseers were Ie and Obadiah, the Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of Kohath, to oversee; and every Levite, everyone skilled with instruments of song.
verses.34:13: They were also over the burden-bearers and over all those who did the work in every kind of service; and from the Levites there were scribes and judges and gatekeepers.
verses.34:14: And as they were bringing out the silver that had been brought into the house of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.34:15: And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found a book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.34:16: And Shaphan brought the book to the king, and furthermore brought word back to the king, saying, "All the silver that was given is in the hand of your servants who do the work,
verses.34:17: and they have melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and he has delivered it into the hand of the overseers who do the work."
verses.34:18: And Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, "There is a book which Hilkiah the priest gave to me." And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.34:19: And it came to pass, when the king heard the law, that he tore his garments.
verses.34:20: And the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdodom the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Isaiah the servant of the king, saying,
verses.34:21: "Go, inquire of the Lord for me, and for all that is left in Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the Lord that has been kindled among us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of the Lord, to do according to all that is written in this book."
verses.34:22: So Hilkiah and those to whom the king had spoken went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Kathual, the son of Chelles, who kept the commandments—now she dwelt in Jerusalem in Maasanai—and they spoke to her to that effect.
verses.34:23: And she said to them, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: 'Tell the man who sent you to Me:
verses.34:24: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing calamities upon this place, all the words written in the book which was read before the king of Judah,
verses.34:25: because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to foreign gods, that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands; and My wrath has been kindled in this place, and it shall not be quenched.
verses.34:26: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, thus shall you say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: As for the words which you have heard,
verses.34:27: and your heart was penitent, and you humbled yourself before My face when you heard My words against this place and against those who dwell in it, and you humbled yourself before Me, and tore your garments and wept before Me—I also have heard, says the Lord.
verses.34:28: Behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace, and your eyes shall not look upon all the calamities which I am bringing upon this place and upon those who dwell in it.'" And they brought word back to the king.
verses.34:29: Then the king sent and gathered the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:30: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, with all Judah and those who dwelt in Jerusalem, and the priests and the Levites, and all the people from the great to the small; and he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that were found in the house of the Lord.
verses.34:31: And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk before the Lord, and to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul—even the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
verses.34:32: And he caused all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to take a stand; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord, the God of their father.
verses.34:33: And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the land that belonged to the sons of Israel, and caused all who were found in Jerusalem and in Israel to serve the Lord their God all his days; he did not turn aside from following the Lord, the God of his fathers.
verses.35:1: Now Josiah kept the Passover to the Lord his God; and they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.35:2: And he appointed the priests to their watches, and encouraged them for the works of the house of the Lord.
verses.35:3: And he spoke to the Levites who were capable in all Israel, that they should sanctify themselves to the Lord; and they placed the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, had built. And the king said, "It is not for you to bear anything upon your shoulders; now therefore minister to the Lord your God and to His people Israel,
verses.35:4: and prepare yourselves according to your fathers' houses and according to your divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel and by the hand of King Solomon his son;
verses.35:5: and stand in the house according to the divisions of your fathers' houses for your brethren, the sons of the people, and a portion of a father's house for the Levites;
verses.35:6: and slaughter the Passover, and prepare for your brethren, to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses."
verses.35:7: And Josiah contributed to the sons of the people sheep and lambs and kids from the young of the goats, all for the Passover, and for all who were found present, to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand calves; these were from the king's possessions.
verses.35:8: And his rulers contributed to the people, and to the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests, and they gave for the Passover two thousand six hundred sheep and lambs and kids, and three hundred calves.
verses.35:9: And Conaniah, and Benaiah, and Shemaiah, and Nethanel his brother, and Hashabiah, and Joel, and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passover five thousand, and five hundred calves.
verses.35:10: So the service was set in order, and the priests stood in their place, and the Levites in their divisions, according to the command of the king.
verses.35:11: And they slaughtered the Passover; and the priests poured out the blood from their hand, while the Levites skinned them.
verses.35:12: And they prepared the burnt offering to deliver it to them according to the divisions by fathers' houses, to the sons of the people, to offer to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses; and likewise for the morning.
verses.35:13: And they roasted the Passover in fire according to the ordinance; and the holy offerings they boiled in the bronze vessels and in the caldrons, and it prospered; and they ran to all the sons of the people.
verses.35:14: And after they had prepared for them and for the priests—because the priests were occupied in offering up the fat and the burnt offerings until night—the Levites prepared for themselves and for their brethren, the sons of Aaron.
verses.35:15: And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the commands of David, and Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, the prophets of the king; and as for the rulers and the gatekeepers at every gate, it was not for them to depart from the ministry of the holy things, because their brethren the Levites prepared for them.
verses.35:16: So all the service of the Lord was set in order and prepared on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer the burnt offerings upon the altar of the Lord, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.35:17: And the sons of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.35:18: And there had been no Passover like it in Israel; from the days of Samuel the prophet and of every king of Israel, they had not kept such a Passover as Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to the Lord,
verses.35:19: in the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah. Moreover, King Josiah burned up the mediums and the spiritists, and the teraphim and the idols and the karasim that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book which Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the Lord. There was no one like him before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses, nor after him did any arise like him. Yet the Lord did not turn away from the fierceness of His great wrath, with which the Lord was angered in wrath against Judah because of all the ordinances with which Manasseh had provoked Him. And the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from sight, just as I removed Israel, and I have rejected the city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
verses.35:20: And Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates; and King Josiah went out to meet him.
verses.35:21: And he sent messengers to him, saying, "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I have not come against you today to wage war, and God has told me to make haste. Beware of God who is with me, lest He destroy you."
verses.35:22: Yet Josiah did not turn his face from him, but strengthened himself to fight against him, and did not listen to the words of Necho from the mouth of God; and he came to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.35:23: And the archers shot at King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am severely wounded."
verses.35:24: So his servants took him out of the chariot and put him in the second chariot that he had, and brought him to Jerusalem. And he died, and was buried with his fathers; and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
verses.35:25: And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the rulers and the female rulers spoke a lament over Josiah to this day; and they made it an ordinance in Israel, and behold, it is written in the Laments.
verses.35:26: Now the acts of Josiah and his hope were written in the law of the Lord,
verses.35:27: and his deeds, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.36:1: Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and they anointed him and appointed him as king in place of his father.
verses.36:2: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Abital, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done. And Pharaoh Necho bound him in Dablatha in the land of Hamath, so that he would not reign in Jerusalem.
verses.36:3: And the king removed him to Egypt, and imposed a tribute upon the land of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.36:4: And Pharaoh Necho appointed Eliakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. And Pharaoh Necho took his brother Jehoahaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there. And he gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; at that time the land began to be taxed to give the silver at the command of Pharaoh, and each one according to his ability exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land to give to Pharaoh Necho.
verses.36:5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Zechora, the daughter of Neriah from Ramah. And he did evil before the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done. In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came into the land, and he served him three years, and rebelled against him. And the Lord sent against him the Chaldeans, and raiding bands of Syrians, and raiding bands of Moabites, and of the sons of Ammon, and of Samaria; and they departed after this word, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of His servants the prophets. Yet the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah, to remove him from His presence because of Manasseh, for all that he had done, and for the innocent blood which Jehoiakim shed; he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the Lord was not willing to destroy them.
verses.36:6: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him, and bound him in bronze fetters, and led him away to Babylon.
verses.36:7: And he carried away a portion of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon, and placed them in his temple in Babylon.
verses.36:8: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and was buried in Ganozae with his fathers. And Jeconiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.36:9: Jeconiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.36:10: And at the return of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him into Babylon with the precious vessels of the house of the Lord; and he made Zedekiah, his father's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.36:11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
verses.36:12: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord his God; he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, nor at the mouth of the Lord,
verses.36:13: in that he set aside his obligations toward King Nebuchadnezzar, which he had made him swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart, so that he would not return to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.36:14: And all the nobles of Judah, and the priests, and the people of the land, transgressed exceedingly with the faithless deeds of the abominations of the nations, and defiled the house of the Lord which was in Jerusalem.
verses.36:15: And the Lord God of their fathers sent by hand, rising early and sending His messengers, because He had compassion on His people and His sanctuary.
verses.36:16: But they mocked His messengers, and despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against His people, until there was no healing.
verses.36:17: And He brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he slew their young men with the sword in the house of His sanctuary; and he did not spare Zedekiah, and they showed no mercy to their virgins, and they led away their elders; He delivered all things into their hands.
verses.36:18: And all the vessels of the house of God, both great and small, and the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and of the nobles—all of them he brought into Babylon.
verses.36:19: And he burned the house of the Lord, and tore down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned her palaces with fire, and brought every beautiful vessel to destruction.
verses.36:20: And he carried the remnant away into Babylon, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the reign of the Medes,
verses.36:21: to fulfill the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land received its Sabbaths to keep Sabbath, to the completion of seventy years.
verses.36:22: In the first year of the king of the Persians, after the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he commanded a proclamation to be made throughout all his kingdom in writing, saying,
verses.36:23: "Thus says Cyrus, king of the Persians, to all the kingdoms of the earth: The Lord God of heaven has given them to me, and He Himself has commanded me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem in Judea. Who is among you of all His people? His God shall be with him, and let him go up."

notes.1:9: The Greek text reads "Your name" (to onoma sou) rather than the Masoretic Text's "Your word."
notes.1:13: The Greek text transliterates and transposes the Hebrew word for "high place" (bamah) as the place-name "Maba," and reads "that is in Jerusalem" rather than "to Jerusalem."
notes.1:14: The Greek text reads "and the people were with the king in Jerusalem," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants for "with" and "people."
notes.1:16: The Greek text interprets the obscure Hebrew term (often understood as the region Kue or a drove of horses) as "price" (time) and renders the closing clause literally.
notes.2:5: The Greek text adds "His glory" (autou ten doxan), stating that the heavens cannot bear God's glory.
notes.2:9: Unlike the Masoretic Text, the Greek text omits oil from Solomon's list of provisions here, though Hiram mentions oil in verse 14.
notes.2:12: "Hiram my father" renders the Greek literally, reflecting the Hebrew honorific title Huram-abi (denoting a master craftsman or esteemed counselor).
notes.2:16: "Sojourners" translates Greek proselytous (proselytes), the standard Septuagint rendering of Hebrew gerim (resident foreigners).
notes.3:1: The Greek text preserves the proper-name forms "Amoria" (incorporating the Hebrew definite article into Moriah) and "Orna" (for Ornan/Araunah).
notes.3:8: The Greek text adds "for the cherubim" (eis cheroubein), linking the six hundred talents of pure gold to both the Holy of Holies and the cherubim.
notes.3:11: Verse 12 is absent in the Greek critical text due to an early scribal skip between the parallel clauses describing the wings of the two cherubim.
notes.3:16: "Chains" and "the inner sanctuary" translate the Greek transliterations serseroth and dabeir from Hebrew.
notes.3:17: Rather than transliterating the Hebrew pillar names Jachin and Boaz, the Greek text translates their meanings as Katorthosis ("Establishment") and Ischys ("Strength").
notes.4:3: The Greek reads "ten cubits encompass the laver all around" (where the Hebrew has "ten to a cubit") and uses gene ("kinds") where the Hebrew has "rows."
notes.4:12: Here and in verses 13, 14, and 20, the Greek retains transliterated Hebrew architectural terms (golath "bowls," chothareth "capitals," mechonoth "stands," and dabeir "inner sanctuary"), and specifies "the tops of the capitals."
notes.4:13: The Greek reads "four hundred golden bells" (where the Hebrew has "four hundred pomegranates") and refers to "kinds of pomegranates" without specifying "two."
notes.4:17: The Greek reads "in the house of Succoth and Anamesirdathai," a distinctive Septuagint form corresponding to the Hebrew "between Succoth and Zeredathah."
notes.4:22: The concluding clause ("And all the work which Solomon made in the house of the Lord was finished") stands at the end of chapter 4 in the Greek, corresponding to the beginning of 5:1 in the Hebrew.
notes.5:6: The Greek includes "and those who feared" alongside "those of them who were gathered together," a distinctive Septuagint reading not present in the Hebrew.
notes.5:9: The Greek states that the ends of the poles were seen "from the holy place" before the inner sanctuary (Greek dabeir), where the Hebrew reads "from the ark."
notes.5:10: The Greek uses a neuter plural relative pronoun ("the things which the Lord covenanted") and specifies "out of the land of Egypt."
notes.5:13: The Greek reads neuter agathon ("for it is good") rather than masculine agathos ("for He is good"), and concludes with "a cloud of the glory of the Lord."
notes.6:2: The Greek reads "a house for Your name, holy to You and prepared to dwell in forever," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "house of habitation."
notes.6:6: The Greek omits the first clause of the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Yet I have chosen Jerusalem, that My name may be there"), moving directly to the choice of David.
notes.6:16: The Greek reads "to walk in My name" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to walk in My law."
notes.6:30: The Greek reads "and heal" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and forgive."
notes.6:41: The Greek reads "Your sons" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Your godly ones," and similarly in 6:42 reads "do not turn away Your face" rather than "the face of Your anointed one."
notes.7:3: The Greek uses the neuter "For it is good" (indicating that praising the Lord is good) rather than the masculine "For He is good."
notes.7:5: The Greek mentions only twenty-two thousand calves and omits the one hundred twenty thousand sheep found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:7: "The grain offerings" renders the Greek transliterated loanword manaa (from Hebrew minhah).
notes.7:13: The Greek reads "to devour the trees" (literally "the wood") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "to devour the land."
notes.7:20: The Greek shifts to the third person ("which I gave to them") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the second person ("which I gave to you").
notes.8:3: The Greek text reads "Baisoba" (and in v. 6 "Baalah"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Hamath-zobah" (and in v. 6 "Baalath").
notes.8:8: The Greek reads "with him" and omits the negative particle before "utterly destroyed," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "after them, whom the sons of Israel had not destroyed."
notes.8:17: The Greek reads "Elam" (and in v. 18 "Sophira"), corresponding to Hebrew "Eloth" (and "Ophir").
notes.9:4: The Greek reads "the burnt offerings which he offered in the house of the Lord," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "his ascent by which he went up to the house of the Lord."
notes.9:10: The Greek reads "Suphir" (for Hebrew "Ophir") and "pine wood" (where Hebrew reads "algum wood"; so also in v. 11).
notes.9:25: The Greek reads "four thousand mares for chariots," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "four thousand stalls for horses and chariots."
notes.9:26: "Foreigners" translates the Greek allophyloi, the Septuagint's standard rendering for the Philistines.
notes.9:29: The Greek reads "Joel the seer," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Iddo the seer."
notes.10:11: Both here and in v. 14, the Greek text reads "our yoke" rather than "your yoke."
notes.10:15: The Greek introduces a direct statement ("saying, 'The Lord has established His word...'") continuing into v. 16, whereas the Hebrew expresses purpose ("in order that the Lord might fulfill His word").
notes.10:17: The Greek text names "Jeroboam" rather than "Rehoboam" as the king who reigned over them.
notes.10:18: The Greek reads "Adoniram" (where the Hebrew reads "Hadoram") and again names "King Jeroboam" rather than "King Rehoboam" as fleeing to Jerusalem.
notes.11:6: The Greek text reads Bethseem and Apan where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Bethlehem and Etam.
notes.11:10: The Greek text reads Aldon where the Hebrew reads Aijalon.
notes.11:16: The Greek text reads "and he cast them out from the tribes of Israel," whereas the Hebrew reads "and after them, from all the tribes of Israel."
notes.11:18: The Greek reads Baia the daughter of Elian (omitting "and" before her name), where the Hebrew reads "and Abihail the daughter of Eliab"; in verses 19–20 the Greek similarly preserves distinct forms Jaouth, Roollam, Jethei, and Emmoth.
notes.11:21: The Greek text reads thirty concubines, whereas the Hebrew reads sixty concubines.
notes.11:23: The Greek reads "he was exalted above all his sons... and gave them [the fortified cities] provisions," differing from the Hebrew, which describes Rehoboam acting wisely and dispersing his sons.
notes.12:3: The Greek reads sixty thousand horses (Hebrew: horsemen) and identifies the second allied people as Troglodytes (Hebrew: Sukkiim).
notes.12:10: In the Greek text, Shishak appoints captains of the runners over Rehoboam, whereas the Hebrew states that Rehoboam committed the bronze shields to the captains of the guard.
notes.12:11: The Greek describes the guards and runners entering and returning to meet the runners, without the Hebrew mention of bearing the shields and returning them to the guardroom.
notes.12:15: The Greek reads "and his deeds" where the Hebrew reads "according to genealogies."
notes.13:1: The Greek text reads "over Israel" where the Hebrew reads "over Judah."
notes.13:4: The Greek reads Mount Somoron where the Hebrew reads Mount Zemaraim.
notes.13:12: The Greek reads "over us" (Hebrew: against you) and "our fathers" (Hebrew: your fathers), and omits the negative particle before "fight" (Hebrew: do not fight), rendered here as a rhetorical question.
notes.13:19: The Greek reads Cana where the Hebrew reads Jeshanah.
notes.13:23: In the Greek text this verse concludes chapter thirteen (corresponding to 14:1 in Hebrew numbering), reads "died" rather than "slept," and adds "of Judah" after "the land."
notes.14:5: The Greek text lacks a verb before "fortified cities" (likely omitted by scribal eye-skip after "had peace" in v. 4), where the Hebrew and some manuscripts supply "he built."
notes.14:8: The Greek reads simply "with thousands" rather than the Hebrew "a thousand thousands" (one million), and renders the town name as Marisel (contrast Mareshah in v. 9).
notes.14:12: The Greek reads "Gedor" here and in v. 13, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Gerar."
notes.14:14: The Greek adds "the Amazoneis" in apposition to "the tents of livestock," a distinctive Septuagint rendering differing from the Hebrew text.
notes.15:2: The Greek reads "while we are with Him" (first person plural) rather than the Hebrew "while you are with Him," and places Judah and Benjamin in the narrative rather than as direct address.
notes.15:4: The Greek renders the verb transitively and in the future tense ("He will turn them back"), omitting the Hebrew phrase "in their distress."
notes.15:8: The Greek names the prophet "Adad" here (contrast "Oded" in v. 1) and reads "the temple of the Lord" where the Hebrew has "the vestibule of the Lord."
notes.15:16: The Greek states that Asa removed Maachah "from ministering to Astarte," differing from the Hebrew "from being queen mother because she had made an abominable image for Asherah."
notes.16:1: The Greek reads "thirty-eighth year" here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thirty-sixth year."
notes.16:2: The Greek renders the Syrian royal name Ben-hadad as "the son of Hader" (here and in v. 4).
notes.16:4: The Greek transmits the northern Israelite town names as Io, Dano, and Abelman (corresponding to Hebrew Ijon, Dan, and Abel-maim) and reads "surrounding regions" for Hebrew "store-cities."
notes.16:7: The Greek names the prophet "Hanami" (Hebrew "Hanani the seer"), and in v. 8 reads "in boldness" where the Hebrew reads "with chariots."
notes.16:13: The Greek text reads "thirtieth year" despite placing Asa's illness in the "thirty-ninth year" in v. 12; the Hebrew and other manuscripts read "forty-first year."
notes.17:7: The Greek renders the Hebrew name Ben-Hail literally as "the sons of the mighty men" and reads the distinct name "Abiah" where the Hebrew reads "Obadiah."
